 ATP Almaty Day 3 Predictions Including Stefanos Tsitsipas vs Mikhail Kukushkin 
 Share Share this article
 × X Facebook LinkedIn WhatsApp Reddit Email Copy 
 Six matches are scheduled for Day 3 in Kazakhstan as the ATP 250 event in Almaty continues with three former finalists in action. We examine three matches in this piece, including a match between 2022 finalist Stefanos Tsitsipas and veteran home favorite Mikhail Kukushkin, who could be playing his final match before he hangs up his racket. Who will advance?
 ATP Almaty Day 3 Predictions
 Tomas Machac vs Zangar Nurlanuly
 Head–to–Head: First Meeting
 Eighteen-year-old Zangar Nurlanuly gets his big moment in Almaty, where a wild card hands him a Tour-level main draw debut. His best result this season is a semifinal run at a lower-level event in Astana, so this is a huge step up in pace and pressure. Across the net is Tomas Machac, a man with a title already in his 2026 trophy cabinet and far more big-match experience in his locker.
 The 26-year-old’s season has been stop-start, with injury once again getting in the way. He ended a main draw drought at the Shanghai Masters with a comeback win over Zhizhen Zhang, his first at that level since Roland Garros, before falling to Alexander Bublik. Rhythm and fitness are the only real questions here. If Machac is healthy, he should have far too much quality for the home hope, and the crowd’s noise may only carry Nurlanuly so far.
 Prediction: Machac in 2 
 Tomas Martin Etcheverry vs Mattia Bellucci
 Head–to–Head : Etcheverry 0 – 1 Bellucci
 Mattia Bellucci arrives in Almaty as one of the Tour’s in-form players. He’s just lifted the Challenger trophy in Jinan, dropping no sets until the final, where he beat Martin Landaluce 6-2 4-6 6-3. It was his second final of the month after a strong run in Jinan, and he’s won 14 of his last 15 matches, including qualifying rounds. Few players in the draw can match that level of match toughness.
 His reward is a first-round meeting with Tomas Martin Etcheverry, who is struggling. The Argentine lost to Dalibor Svrcina in Shanghai, stretching his losing run to four matches. Outside his round-of-16 run at the US Open, he has gone out in the opening round of his last six events. Bellucci also holds a 1-0 head-to-head lead, having come from a set down to win their Italian Open meeting. Etcheverry is the higher-ranked man, but with confidence this low and Bellucci riding a wave of results, the 25-year-old Italian looks the likelier winner.
 Prediction: Bellucci in 3 
 Jul 29, 2024; Washington, DC, USA; Mattia Bellucci (ITA) hits a backhand against Mackenzie McDonald (USA)(not pictured) on day three of the Mubadala Citi DC Open at Rock Creek Park Tennis Center. Mandatory Credit: Geoff Burke-USA TODAY Sports 
 Stefanos Tsitsipas vs Mikhail Kukushkin
 Head–to–Head: Tsitsipas 5 – 0 Kukushkin
 Stefanos Tsitsipas is through to the next round in Almaty, but he had to work for it. The former World #3 edged a 7-6(9) first-set tiebreak against Aleksandar Kovacevic, dropped the second 6-3, then steadied himself to close it out 6-3 in the decider. The tournament already holds a special place for him: his only previous appearance, in 2022, ended in a final loss to Novak Djokovic. A scrappy opener won’t dent the confidence of a player who knows he can go deep here.
 Next up is Mikhail Kukushkin, and the occasion belongs to the 39-year-old. He is retiring after this event, and he bought himself at least one more match by beating Stefanos Sakellaridis with both sets going to tiebreaks. The sentiment will be loud, but the numbers aren’t on his side: Tsitsipas leads the head-to-head 5-0, including a 6-3 6-4 win at this very tournament four years ago. I expect more of the same: a clean, controlled win for the two-time Grand Slam finalist that builds his momentum and sends Kukushkin off with applause rather than a result.
 Prediction: Tsitsipas in 2
